title: Minimum Distance to the Target Element
summary: In an integer array nums, locate an index i where nums[i] equals the target and the absolute difference between i and the start index is minimal.
statement: In an integer array nums, locate an index i where nums[i] equals the target and the absolute difference between i and the start index is minimal. Return this minimal difference.
constraints: target occurs at least once and start is a valid index.
Return the minimum absolute index distance from start to an occurrence of target.
reference_solution:
def minimum_target_distance(nums, target, start):
 return min(abs(index-start) for index,value in enumerate(nums) if value==target)
hints: Every occurrence is an independent candidate.
Scan indices whose value equals target and measure abs(index-start).
Absolute difference is exactly the number of index steps, and taking the minimum over every occurrence cannot miss the nearest one.
editorial: Absolute difference is exactly the number of index steps, and taking the minimum over every occurrence cannot miss the nearest one.

tests.explanation: Target five is at index four, one step from start index three.
The start position already equals target, so distance is zero.
